I build clinical prediction models that can be checked: properly evaluated,
calibrated, audited for how they perform across different patient groups, and
reported transparently enough that someone else can reproduce them. I write
my analyses as reproducible pipelines in line with the NHS Reproducible
Analytical Pipelines (RAP) approach and publish the code.

Before moving into data science I spent eight years at OxSTaR, the simulation
and training centre at the John Radcliffe Hospital in Oxford, building the data
systems and technology behind clinical training. I have run an independent
consultancy since 2012.

My MSc thesis used accelerometry data from the Millennium Cohort Study to
examine how the duration and temporal structure of activity recordings affect
ADHD prediction, comparing interpretable and complex models and testing for
bias across subgroups. See [Projects](projects.qmd).

## Interests

Clinical prediction modelling · Model evaluation and calibration ·
Algorithmic fairness · Reproducible analytical pipelines · Neurodevelopmental
conditions
